`CONTRIBUTING.md`:

```md
# Contributing

Pull requests are welcome: bug fixes, new input or capture paths, better OCR / matching, MCP tools, docs.

## Scope: offline games only

This project is for single-player / offline games. Contributions that help bypass, hide from, or work around
anti-cheat systems, that target online or multiplayer games, or that weaken or remove the anti-cheat refusal
(`src/vi_acguard.h`) will not be accepted. Adding more anti-cheat names to the refusal lists is very welcome.

## Every change comes with a red/green test

- Add or extend a test that **fails on the code before your change and passes after it** (a red/green pair), and say
  in the PR how you saw it red - for example by running the test against a build of `main` with `-CliDir`.
- Tests use the **synthetic targets** in `test/` (they log what they receive, so the test checks the target's view,
  not only vinput's reply). Real games cannot be part of the automated suite; if you verified something in a real game,
  describe it in the PR (game, API, what you checked), but keep game-specific files out of the repository.
- Clean up: tests stop only the processes they started, by PID.
- Run before you open the PR:

  ```bat
  build.bat                                   &rem x64 + x86, must build with 0 warnings
  pwsh -File verify\run_selftest.ps1          &rem full suite, PowerShell 7
  cd mcp && npm ci && npm run build && npm test && npm run smoke
  ```

## Style

- C++17 / C++20 with MSVC, `/W3` clean, no new external dependencies without discussion (vendored code goes into
  `third_party/` with its licence and an entry in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`).
- Every CLI command answers one JSON line with `ok`; errors are explicit, never silent.
- Keep the game's own threads fast: no blocking waits in hooks on the present path.
- Documentation changes go with the code change (`README.md`, `docs/CLI.md`, `mcp/README.md`).

## Reporting bugs

Use the issue templates. Include the vinput reply JSON, `status` output, the DLL log (`dist\run\logs\vinput_<pid>.log`)
and the graphics API / engine of the game. Do not report problems with online or anti-cheat protected games.

```

`DISCLAIMER.md`:

```md
# Disclaimer

**Read this before you use LLM Game Automation MCP (vinput).**

1. **Single-player / offline games only.** This project exists to automate, test and play games that run entirely on
   your own machine.
2. **Do not use it in online or multiplayer games, or with any game protected by anti-cheat.** Injecting code into
   such a game breaks its terms of service and will very likely get your account banned. Automating other players'
   experience is not what this project is for.
3. **It injects a DLL into the target process.** `vinput.exe` loads `vinput64.dll` / `vinput32.dll` into the game and
   hooks Windows input, focus and graphics APIs inside that process. Security software may flag this, and a game can
   behave differently or crash with foreign code in it. Back up your saves first.
4. **The anti-cheat refusal is a courtesy, not a guarantee.** vinput refuses to inject when it recognises a known
   anti-cheat (EasyAntiCheat, BattlEye, Riot Vanguard, Ricochet, FACEIT, ESEA, nProtect GameGuard, XIGNCODE3,
   ACE / AntiCheatExpert, PunkBuster, mhyprot, Denuvo Anti-Cheat) loaded in the game, installed next to it, or
   running on the machine. The check is name-based and best-effort: a renamed, new or unlisted anti-cheat will not be
   detected. **It is your responsibility** to make sure a game is offline and unprotected before you point this tool
   at it. The refusal has no override flag; please do not patch it out.
5. **Use at your own risk.** The software is provided "as is", without warranty of any kind (see `LICENSE`). The
   authors and contributors are not responsible for account bans, lost or corrupted saves, data loss, crashes,
   damage to your system, violations of any terms of service, or anything else that results from using it.
6. **LLM agents act on their own.** When an AI agent drives a game through the MCP server, it can press keys and click
   things you did not anticipate (spend in-game currency, overwrite a save, quit without saving). Supervise it, and
   only give it games where such mistakes are acceptable.

```

`README.md`:

```md
# LLM Game Automation MCP

> [!WARNING]
> **Single-player / offline games only.** Do **not** use this in online or multiplayer games, or with any game
> protected by anti-cheat: you will very likely be banned. **It injects a DLL into the target game process.**
> vinput refuses to inject when it detects a known anti-cheat, but that check is a courtesy, not a guarantee.
> **Use at your own risk**: the authors are not responsible for bans, lost saves, data loss, damage or anything else
> that results from using it. Read [DISCLAIMER.md](DISCLAIMER.md) first.

Let an LLM agent (or a script) play Windows games **in the background**. Each game process gets its own private
keyboard, mouse, gamepad and eyes:

- **vinput** - a DLL injected into one game process plus a CLI (`vinput.exe`) that talks to it over a per-process
  named pipe. Input is delivered *inside* that process on every channel games read; frames are captured from the
  game's own swapchain.
- **MCP server** (`mcp/`) - wraps the CLI as [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) tools
  (`launch`, `capture`, `click_text`, `key`, `pad`, ...), so Claude or any MCP client can look at a game and act on it.

## Why it is different

Most "AI plays games" setups drive the real desktop: `SendInput` plus a screenshot of the whole screen. That needs the
game in front, steals your mouse and keyboard, and allows exactly one game at a time. vinput works per process:

- **The game never needs focus.** It keeps running and rendering in the background; vinput fakes focus inside the game
  and swallows its deactivation messages.
- **You keep your PC.** vinput never generates OS-level input (no `SendInput`); your real typing is hidden from a
  background game, and the game cannot steal the foreground from you.
- **Several games at once.** Every game has its own pipe and command queue, so several agents can drive several
  games in parallel, each with an optional ownership claim.
- **Pixels from the game itself.** Captures come from the frame the game presents (not a desktop screenshot), so they
  work while the window is covered by other windows.

## Supported APIs

| | supported | notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Capture** | Direct3D 11, Direct3D 12, OpenGL, Vulkan, `PrintWindow` fallback | HDR formats (R10G10B10A2, RGBA16F) converted to 8-bit; Vulkan needs early injection (`launch --early`); D3D9/D3D10 fall back to `PrintWindow` |
| **Keyboard** | window messages (`WM_KEYDOWN`/`WM_CHAR`, with the game's own `TranslateMessage`), Raw Input (`WM_INPUT`, `GetRawInputBuffer` on x64), DirectInput 8 and legacy `dinput.dll` (DirectInput 1-7), `GetAsyncKeyState`/`GetKeyState`/`GetKeyboardState` | mirrors the game's own `RegisterRawInputDevices` choices (e.g. `RIDEV_NOLEGACY`) |
| **Mouse** | messages, Raw Input, DirectInput 8, virtual cursor behind `GetCursorPos` / `WindowFromPoint` | absolute (`click`, `move`) and relative (`move_relative`, mouse-look) |
| **Gamepad** | XInput pad 0 (`XInputGetState`, `XInputGetStateEx`) | buttons, both sticks, triggers |
| **Vision (CLI side)** | Windows OCR (`Windows.Media.Ocr`), normalised cross-correlation template matching | runs in the CLI, nothing extra is loaded into the game |
| **Targets** | 64-bit and 32-bit games, UWP / Xbox-app (AppContainer) games | `vinput.exe` hands 32-bit targets to `vinput32.exe` |

## Requirements

- Windows 10 or 11, x64.
- To build: Visual Studio 2022 or newer (or the Build Tools) with the **Desktop development with C++** workload (x64
  and x86 compilers).
- For the MCP server: Node.js 20 or newer.
- The game should run **windowed or borderless**. Exclusive fullscreen loses its swapchain as soon as another window is
  in front.

## Build

```bat
build.bat
```

`build.bat` finds MSVC through `vswhere`; set `VINPUT_VCVARS_DIR` to a `...\VC\Auxiliary\Build` folder to pick a
specific install. It builds x64 and x86 into `dist\` (git-ignored): `vinput.exe`, `vinput32.exe`, `vinput64.dll`,
`vinput32.dll`, `vinput_x64.lib`, `vinput_x86.lib` and the synthetic test targets. MinHook and the Vulkan headers are
vendored in `third_party\`, so nothing else is downloaded.

MCP server:

```bat
cd mcp
npm ci
npm run build
npm test
```

`npm test` is the MCP handshake test (`tools/list` against the built server); it needs no game. Self-tests: see
[TESTING.md](TESTING.md).

## CLI quick start

```bat
rem start a game and inject (prints {"ok":true,"pid":1234,...})
dist\vinput.exe launch --exe "C:\Games\MyGame\MyGame.exe" --args "-windowed"

rem or inject into a game that is already running
dist\vinput.exe inject --pid 1234

dist\vinput.exe --pid 1234 capture shot.png
dist\vinput.exe --pid 1234 click-text "New Game"
dist\vinput.exe --pid 1234 wait-text "Choose difficulty"
dist\vinput.exe --pid 1234 key enter
dist\vinput.exe --pid 1234 hold w 1500
dist\vinput.exe --pid 1234 click left 480 300
dist\vinput.exe --pid 1234 pad a
dist\vinput.exe --pid 1234 status
```

`capture` saves the game's own frame; `click-text` / `wait-text` act on and verify on-screen text (OCR); `hold w 1500`
holds W for 1.5 s; coordinates are client pixels, which equal capture pixels; `pad` drives XInput pad 0; `status`
shows, among other things, which input APIs the game really reads.

Every command prints one JSON line; exit code 0 means `"ok":true`. `ok:true` on an input command means the input was
delivered, **not** that the game reacted: follow it with `wait-text`, `wait-change` or a capture. Full reference:
[docs/CLI.md](docs/CLI.md).

## MCP quick start

Build the server (above), then add it to your MCP client. Claude Code:

```bat
claude mcp add game-automation -- node C:\path\to\llm-game-automation-mcp\mcp\build\index.js
```

Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`) or any stdio MCP client:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "game-automation": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["C:\\path\\to\\llm-game-automation-mcp\\mcp\\build\\index.js"]
    }
  }
}
```

Then ask the agent to launch a game and play it. The tools, their schemas and a short agent quick start are in
[mcp/README.md](mcp/README.md).

## How it works (inside the game process)

| part | how |
|---|---|
| fake focus | `GetForegroundWindow` / `GetActiveWindow` / `GetFocus` report the game; the game's window procedure is subclassed and deactivation (`WM_ACTIVATEAPP(0)`, `WM_ACTIVATE(WA_INACTIVE)`, `WM_NCACTIVATE(0)`, `WM_KILLFOCUS`) is swallowed, so it keeps running and rendering in the background |
| no focus stealing | while the game is not really in front, `SetForegroundWindow` / `BringWindowToTop` / `SetActiveWindow` are no-ops, `SetWindowPos` gets `SWP_NOACTIVATE`, showing the window does not activate it, `ClipCursor` / `SetCursorPos` never touch the real cursor, DXGI exclusive fullscreen is refused; every attempt is logged |
| virtual input | each event is delivered on every channel the game can read, as a real key would be (see Supported APIs) |
| isolation | while the game is not really in front, the real keyboard and mouse are hidden from it, so your typing elsewhere does not leak into it; when it is in front, real input works and virtual input is added on top |
| eyes | native capture from the game's swapchain (per API), with `PrintWindow` as the fallback; replies report `capture_path` and the frame number |
| control | named pipe `\\.\pipe\vinput_<pid>`, one JSON object per line; `vinput.exe` wraps it |
| anti-cheat refusal | `src/vi_acguard.h`: the CLI refuses to inject, and the DLL refuses to start or keep working, when a known anti-cheat is detected (see below) |

## Anti-cheat refusal

Before it injects anything, vinput refuses - with `{"ok":false,"anticheat_refused":true,...}`, exit code 4 and
**no override flag** - when:

1. the target process has a module loaded whose name belongs to a known anti-cheat;
2. the game's folder (or up to three parent folders) ships a known anti-cheat component, e.g. an `EasyAntiCheat` or
   `BattlEye` folder or `start_protected_game.exe` (this catches a protected game before its anti-cheat loads, and
   is checked before `launch --exe` starts anything);
3. a known anti-cheat process is running, or a known anti-cheat service or kernel driver is active, anywhere on the
   machine.

The injected DLL repeats check 1 when it starts, and watches module loads: if an anti-cheat module is loaded into the
game later, every input and capture command is refused from then on.

Covered by name: EasyAntiCheat, BattlEye, Riot Vanguard (vgc / vgk), Ricochet, FACEIT, ESEA, nProtect GameGuard,
XIGNCODE3, ACE (AntiCheatExpert), PunkBuster, mhyprot, Denuvo Anti-Cheat. The lists are in `src/vi_acguard.h`.

**This is defence in depth, not a guarantee.** It is name-based: a renamed, new or unlisted anti-cheat is not
detected, and an absent refusal does not mean a game is safe to automate. Because check 3 is machine-wide, a kernel
anti-cheat that stays resident (for example Vanguard's `vgc` service) blocks vinput until it is stopped.

## Limitations

- **Exclusive fullscreen** is not supported (run windowed / borderless); a **minimised** game stops rendering (vinput
  puts a background game back unless `config keepvisible=false`).
- **Inputs vinput does not reach:** direct syscall / `NtUserGetAsyncKeyState` readers; Windows.Gaming.Input,
  GameInput and WinRT `CoreWindow` keyboard events (many UWP games: use `pad`); HID read directly; DirectInput
  joysticks; Steam Input; `GetRawInputBuffer` in 32-bit processes; XInput users 1-3.
- **Capture:** Vulkan only when vinput is injected before the game creates its device (`launch --early`); D3D9 and
  D3D10 are not captured natively; `PrintWindow` can be black or white for some surfaces.
- **OCR** has no confidence score and can misread stylised or very small text: use `--region`, `--scale 2` or image
  matching. Image matching does not handle rotation and finds scales within about +-20 % by default.
- **Text:** `type` posts `WM_CHAR` (right for text boxes); games that only read raw keys need `type --keys`, which does
  not apply Shift for punctuation yet.
- The game can still be brought to the front by **other** programs; while it is really in front it receives the real
  keyboard.
- vinput stays loaded in a game until the game exits.
- Verified live on a set of commercial D3D11, D3D12 (UWP) and OpenGL games; **Vulkan has only been verified on the
  synthetic test target**, not in a real game. See [TESTING.md](TESTING.md).

## Repository layout

```
src/            vinput DLL (vinput_core.cpp; capture: vi_cap12.h vi_capgl.h vi_capvk.h), CLI (vinput_cli.cpp, vi_cli_*.inl),
                anti-cheat refusal (vi_acguard.h), OCR / text / image matching (vi_ocr.h vi_text.h vi_ncc.h vi_vision.h)
test/           synthetic targets: input logger, D3D12 / GL / Vulkan / XInput targets, UI menu target, anti-cheat refusal target
verify/         PowerShell self-tests (run_selftest.ps1 runs the suite)
macros/         example .vin scripts for the synthetic UI target
mcp/            the MCP server (TypeScript)
third_party/    MinHook, Khronos Vulkan headers (with their licences)
docs/CLI.md     full CLI reference
```

## Compiling vinput into your own DLL

Instead of injecting `vinput64.dll`, you can link `dist\vinput_x64.lib` (or `vinput_x86.lib`) into a DLL of your own:
compile with `/DVINPUT_COMPILE_IN /I<repo>\src`, link `d3d11.lib dxgi.lib dxguid.lib windowscodecs.lib ole32.lib`,
`#include "vinput.h"` and call `VINPUT_INIT();` from your init (safe in `DllMain`; it only starts a thread). Without
the define `VINPUT_INIT()` compiles to nothing. vinput's MinHook is renamed (`VIMH_*`), so it links next to your own
MinHook, and both hook chains work. If `vinput64.dll` is also injected, the second copy is a no-op. The anti-cheat
start-up check runs in this mode too.

`SECURITY.md`:

```md
# Security policy

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please **do not open a public issue** for a security problem. Use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting
("Security" tab -> "Report a vulnerability") on this repository. Include what you found, how to reproduce it, and the
impact you expect. You should get an answer within a few days; please allow time for a fix before disclosing.

## What counts

- The control pipe (`\\.\pipe\vinput_<pid>`) letting another user, a lower-integrity process or a remote machine drive
  or read a game it should not.
- The CLI or the MCP server executing something other than what it was asked (argument injection, path handling).
- The MCP server exposing more than the documented tools, or file access beyond the paths it is given.
- A way to make the anti-cheat refusal pass silently for a target that the lists in `src/vi_acguard.h` do cover.

## What does not count

- That vinput injects a DLL and hooks APIs in the target process: that is what it does (see `DISCLAIMER.md`).
- That the anti-cheat refusal misses an anti-cheat it does not list: it is a best-effort courtesy, not a security
  boundary. Pull requests adding names are welcome.
- Security products flagging DLL injection.

## Design notes

- The pipe is created per game process and is reachable by the same user; vinput is a local tool for your own games
  and should not be run on a shared or multi-user machine where other users must not control your games.
- vinput never generates OS-level input (`SendInput`) except the explicit `sysinput` test command.
- The MCP server is a local stdio process; it opens no network ports.

```

`TESTING.md`:

```md
# Testing

All automated tests run against **synthetic targets** built from `test/` - small programs that log every input they
receive and draw known pixel patterns - so a test checks what the *target* saw, not only what vinput replied. No real
game is needed, and no test drives the real keyboard or mouse.

## Run

```bat
build.bat
pwsh -File verify\run_selftest.ps1
cd mcp && npm ci && npm run build && npm test && npm run smoke
```

PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`) is required. `run_selftest.ps1` stops at the first failure and stops only the processes it
started, by PID. Test output goes to `build\test\` (git-ignored).

Only `run_fgguardtest.ps1` touches the real foreground (for a few milliseconds, to simulate a game stealing it). It holds
a lock file meanwhile: set `VINPUT_LOCK` to the lock file that other foreground-taking tools on your machine use, or it
uses `build\foreground.lock`. Close fullscreen games before running the suite.

## What is covered

| script | covers |
|---|---|
| `run_selftest.ps1` | every input channel on x64 / x86, injected DLL and compiled-in mode, D3D11 capture, background isolation; then runs the scripts below (except the three standalone ones) |
| `run_clicktest.ps1`, `run_activatetest.ps1`, `run_keytest.ps1`, `run_tracetest.ps1`, `run_movetest.ps1` | hover-gated clicks, focus shims, key names / chords / mouse buttons, per-API key tracing, relative and raw mouse motion |
| `run_overlaycapturetest.ps1` | capture of a DDraw-wrapper style game (game window black or stale, picture in a separate `...PresentationWindow`), x64 and x86 |
| `run_capturetest.ps1`, `run_nativecapture.ps1` | capture regions and frame waits; native D3D12 / OpenGL / Vulkan capture (BGRA, RGBA, R10G10B10A2, RGBA16F; x64 / x86; AppContainer), pixel-exact pattern decode, 50 resizes per API, late-injection refusal for Vulkan |
| `run_xinputtest.ps1` | XInput pad 0: buttons, sticks, triggers, durations, hold, off, Guide via `XInputGetStateEx` |
| `run_actest.ps1` | anti-cheat refusal (below) |
| `run_unittests.ps1`, `run_ocrtest.ps1`, `run_texttest.ps1`, `run_imagetest.ps1`, `run_smalltest.ps1`, `run_scripttest.ps1` | text matching and NCC unit tests (x64 / x86), OCR, click / wait / assert text, image matching, pixel / scroll / drag / unicode type, macro scripts |
| `run_jsontest.ps1`, `run_foregroundtest.ps1`, `run_earlytest.ps1`, `run_multitest.ps1`, `run_fgguardtest.ps1` | JSON output, non-activating launch and foreground hand-back, early (suspended) injection, several clients driving several targets with ownership claims, delayed foreground re-grab |
| standalone: `run_launchtest.ps1`, `run_locktest.ps1`, `run_parsertests.ps1` | launch JSON / lock regressions, JSON lock leases (x64 / x86, `/W4 /WX`), key-name parser |
| `mcp/test/handshake.mjs` (`npm test`) | the built MCP server answers `initialize` and `tools/list`; every tool has a description and an object schema; argument errors come back as `isError` |
| `mcp/test/smoke.mjs` (`npm run smoke`) | end to end through MCP on `vi_uitarget`: launch, capture (image content), wait_text, ocr, find_text, key, click_text, type_text, region capture, status, explicit errors, release, detach, anti-cheat refusal via `attach` - each action checked in the target's own log |

## Anti-cheat refusal test (`verify/run_actest.ps1`)

The "anti-cheat" is `test/vi_acdummy.cpp`: an **empty** DLL that only carries an anti-cheat-like file name
(`EasyAntiCheat_x64.dll`, `BEClient.dll`), plus a copy of the plain target renamed `BEService.exe`. Every refusal is
paired with a positive control showing the same target **is** injectable without the trigger, so a pass cannot come
from a broken injector:

- x64 target with the EasyAntiCheat-named module, x86 target with the BattlEye-named module: `inject` refused (exit 4),
  no vinput module, no control pipe;
- a game folder that ships an `EasyAntiCheat` folder: `launch` and `launch --early` refused before anything starts;
  `inject` into the running copy refused; injectable once the folder is gone;
- a `BEService.exe` process running: `inject` and `launch` refused; injectable once it has exited;
- an anti-cheat module loaded **after** injection: input and capture commands refused from then on, `status` reports
  `anticheat_disabled`, and the target never receives the refused key;
- the DLL loaded directly next to an anti-cheat module: no hooks, no pipe, `REFUSED` in its log.

Run it against an older build with `-CliDir <folder with that vinput.exe>` to see it red.

## Real games

Automated tests cannot include commercial games. During development vinput was also exercised by hand on installed
single-player games (background menus, loading saves, walking, map toggles, two games at once while another window
held the focus): Direct3D 11 games on Unity and Unreal Engine 4, a Direct3D 12 UWP game (capture and XInput pad), and a
Unity game in OpenGL mode (capture). **Vulkan capture has been verified only on the synthetic target, not in a real
game.** OCR on stylised game fonts is read inconsistently from run to run; use regions, `--scale 2` or image matching.

Not verified anywhere: `GetRawInputBuffer` injection (no target uses it), 32-bit real games, D3D9 / D3D10 games.

`docs/CLI.md`:

```md
# vinput CLI reference

`vinput.exe` (x64) injects into and drives one game process; it hands 32-bit targets to `vinput32.exe` automatically.
Every command prints **one JSON line** on stdout and exits 0 when the reply has `"ok":true`. Pass `--json` anywhere for
strictly JSON output (launch progress and script step reports then go to stderr; `--json help` returns the help text in
JSON). Refusals by the anti-cheat check exit with code 4 and carry `"anticheat_refused":true`.

## Reference

```
vinput inject --pid N [--dll PATH]
vinput launch (--exe PATH | --steam APPID --wait-exe NAME.exe | --aumid PFN!AppId) [--args "..."] [--wait-exe NAME.exe]
              [--lock FILE] [--lock-retry 60] [--lock-max-wait S] [--timeout 240] [--settle 5] [--fg-guard 5] [--early]
              [--dll PATH] [--no-inject] [--owner NAME] [--claim-ttl 300]
vinput list                                     pids with a live vinput pipe: exe, owner, uptime, really_foreground
vinput keys                                     every accepted key name and its VK code
vinput [--owner NAME] [--force-claim] --pid N <command>     (owner also from env VINPUT_OWNER)
vinput --owner NAME --pid N claim [--ttl 300] | unclaim
vinput --pid N status | ping | log | activate | release | restore
vinput --pid N key <combo> [ms] [--count N] [--gap ms]     combo: a, enter, esc, space, up, f1, ctrl+s, 0x2D, vk45 ...
vinput --pid N down <combo> | up <combo> | hold <combo> <ms>
vinput --pid N type "text" [--delay ms] [--keys]           WM_CHAR text; --keys = real key presses per character
vinput --pid N mouse <x> <y> [--norm] [--capture-space] [--steps N]
vinput --pid N move <dx> <dy> [--steps N] [--raw]          relative (raw / DirectInput deltas, mouse-look)
vinput --pid N click [left|right|middle|x1|x2] [<x> <y>] [--norm] [--capture-space] [--count N] [--ms 60]
vinput --pid N wheel <delta>
vinput --pid N pad <a+b+x+y+lb+rb+start+back+up+down+left+right+ls+rs+guide|none> [ms] [--lx N --ly N --rx N --ry N --lt N --rt N] [--hold]
vinput --pid N pad off                          stop overriding pad 0
vinput --pid N capture <out.png> [--method auto|native|swapchain|printwindow] [--after-frames N] [--region x,y,w,h]
vinput --pid N wait-change [--region x,y,w,h] [--timeout S]
vinput --pid N trace key <key>
vinput --pid N config fakefocus=true autoactivate=true isolate=true blockfocus=true nofullscreen=true keepvisible=true vk=on|off
                      cursor=auto|virtual|real raw=auto|post|buffer|off msgs=auto|on|off hwnd=0x...
vinput --pid N json '{"cmd":"key","key":"enter","ms":80}'
vinput --pid N ocr [--region x,y,w,h] [--lang L] [--scale S] [--tiles] [--lines-only] [--out f.json]
vinput --pid N click-text "text" [--nth N] [--exact] [--fuzzy N] [--timeout ms] [--button B] [--region R] [--dry-run] [--optional]
vinput --pid N wait-text "text" [--timeout ms] [--gone] [--region R] [--optional]
vinput --pid N assert-text "text" [--absent]
vinput --pid N find-image|click-image|wait-image T.png [--threshold 0.8] [--scales a,b,c|--no-scale] [--region R] [--nth N] [--timeout ms] [--gone] [--dry-run] [--optional]
vinput --pid N pixel X Y
vinput --pid N scroll N [X Y] [--horizontal]
vinput --pid N drag x1 y1 x2 y2 [--ms 300] [--button B]
vinput --pid N script <file> [--continue]
vinput --pid N foreground                       hand-off only: really bring the game to the front
vinput sysinput <vk>                            test only: one OS-level SendInput key (the shared keyboard)
```

Coordinates are client pixels; `--norm` = 0..1 fractions of the client size; `--capture-space` = pixels of the last
capture (after a `--region` capture, its origin is applied). `status.counters` shows which input APIs the game
actually calls (`gaks`, `di_kbd`, `rid`, `rib`, `xinput`, `wm_key`, ...): read it first when a game ignores input.
The DLL logs to `dist\run\logs\vinput_<pid>.log` (or `logs\` next to the DLL that was loaded).

## Launching

`launch` starts the game, waits for its window, injects and lets it settle. It snapshots the current foreground window
first, starts the game with a non-activating hint, and hands the foreground back if the game takes it; replies report
`foreground_restored`.

- **`--lock FILE`** (optional): a cooperative lock file held only while launching (from start until vinput has adopted
  the window, plus the settle and guard time), released on success and on failure. Use the same file for every tool
  on the machine that may take the real foreground, so they do not fight over it. Locks are atomic JSON leases with
  owner / token / file-identity checks on release; an existing lock owned by someone else is never reclaimed, even a
  stale one (`--lock-retry` seconds between attempts, `--lock-max-wait` to give up).
- **`--fg-guard S`** (default 5): some games take the real foreground back after the first restore (for example when a
  launcher dialog closes). `launch` keeps watching for S seconds and hands it back each time, reporting every hand-back
  in `foreground_regrabs[]`. If the game is running and injected but the hand-back failed, the reply is
  `ok:true, foreground_restored:false` plus a `warning` (not `ok:false`, which would invite a duplicate launch).
  `--fg-guard 0` turns it off.
- **`--early`**: the process is created suspended, vinput is injected and its pipe is up before the game's first
  instruction, then the main thread is resumed (`early_injected:true`). vinput also watches DLL loads, so
  `vulkan-1.dll` / `opengl32.dll` are hooked the moment they are mapped. Vulkan capture needs this. Requires `--exe`.
- **Launchers / Steam:** games that restart themselves through a launcher exit immediately when started directly.
  Use `--steam <appid> --wait-exe <Game.exe>` (with no `--args` it uses `steam://rungameid/<appid>`, which shows no
  arguments dialog) or `--wait-exe` with a launcher exe. `--wait-exe` picks the NEW process with that name.
- **UWP / Xbox app games:** `--aumid PFN!AppId` returns the exact PID from the activation manager. The DLL copy and the
  log folder are made readable by the AppContainer; captures are staged in the log folder and moved to the requested
  path. These games often read CoreWindow keyboard events (which vinput does not reach): use `pad`.
- Always attach other tools by **PID**, never by process name.
- `inject` loads a per-build copy of the DLL from `dist\run\`, so `build.bat` can replace `dist\vinput64.dll` while games
  run. `dist\run\` accumulates one copy per build that was injected; delete it when no game uses them.

**Run the game windowed or borderless.** Exclusive fullscreen loses its swapchain when another window is in front;
vinput refuses DXGI `SetFullscreenState(TRUE)` (`DXGI_ERROR_NOT_CURRENTLY_AVAILABLE`, which games must already
handle). Typical switches: Unreal `-windowed -ResX=960 -ResY=540`; Unity `-screen-fullscreen 0 -screen-width 960
-screen-height 540`; otherwise the game's own settings. Do not minimise a game: minimised games stop rendering.

## Several agents, several games

Every game has its own pipe and its own command mutex inside the game process, so agents driving different games never
wait on each other. Commands to one game run one at a time, in order; the read-only commands `ping`, `status`, `log`,
`trace` (and `claim` / `unclaim`) skip that mutex, so `status` answers during a long `--after-frames` capture or wait.

```
vinput --owner agentA --pid N claim --ttl 300     # or env VINPUT_OWNER=agentA; launch --owner agentA claims the new pid
vinput --owner agentA --pid N key enter           # accepted, and extends the claim (sliding TTL)
vinput --owner agentB --pid N key enter           # refused: {"ok":false,"claim_refused":true,"claim_owner":"agentA",...}
vinput --owner agentA --pid N unclaim             # or let it expire; --force-claim overrides (logged in the game)
vinput list                                       # pid, exe, owner, claim_expires_in_ms, uptime_ms, really_foreground
```

A command with no owner is refused by a claimed game too. `status` and `list` are always readable.

## Input details

- `click X Y`, `mousedown X Y`, `mouseup X Y` move the virtual cursor there first, dispatch a hover, and wait three
  presented frames (D3D) or 100 ms before the button goes down, so hover-gated UI accepts the click
  (`--hover-frames N`, `--hover-timeout-ms`, `--settle-ms`). Replies report `cursor`, coordinates and `hover_frames`.
- `move DX DY` sends full raw / DirectInput deltas and clamps the virtual cursor to the client area; `--raw` does not
  clamp (games that compute look from `GetCursorPos` and re-centre with `SetCursorPos`). Replies distinguish
  `applied_dx/dy` (virtual cursor travel) from `raw_dx/dy` (requested deltas).
- Key names are case-insensitive: letters, digits, `enter`, `esc`, `space`, `tab`, arrows, `f1`..`f24`,
  `numpad0`..`numpad9`, `num+`, `num-`, `num*`, `num/`, `oem1`, `oem102`, `VK_OEM_PLUS`, media / browser / IME keys,
  `vk1`..`vk255`, `0x2D`. Chords with `+`: `ctrl+s`, `hold w+space 1500`, `key ctrl+num+`. Mouse buttons work in chords
  too: `lbutton`, `rbutton`, `mbutton`, `xbutton1`, `xbutton2` (`down rbutton`, capture, `up rbutton`). `vinput keys`
  lists everything.
- `type` posts exact `WM_CHAR` per UTF-16 unit (surrogate pairs and non-Latin text work); `--keys` presses real keys.
- `trace key esc` reports per-key injected transitions, dispatched messages and API reads (`GetAsyncKeyState`,
  `GetKeyState`, `GetKeyboardState`, DirectInput state / buffer, raw data / buffer). A message or raw delivery with no
  polling increase shows the game's polling code did not read the key. Counters prove API delivery, not that the game
  performed an action.
- `activate` enables the virtual focus shims only; it does not request the real foreground.
- `config fakefocus=false` stops the focus API overrides and deactivation-message suppression; `isolate` separately
  controls hiding real background input; `keepvisible=false` stops vinput restoring a minimised background game.
- A game whose window procedure has never seen `WM_ACTIVATEAPP(TRUE)` (started in the background) is sent the activation
  messages a real switch would send (`WM_NCACTIVATE`, `WM_ACTIVATEAPP`, `WM_ACTIVATE`, `WM_SETFOCUS`), posted to its own
  window, while `fakefocus` and `blockfocus` are on and it is not really foreground. Games that keep their own "active"
  flag (Fallout 1/2 and other DirectDraw-era titles) otherwise ignore all input. The real foreground does not change;
  `status` shows `app_active` and the `act_synth` counter. `config autoactivate=false` turns it off.

## Capture

`capture shot.png` saves the game's frame and reports `method`, `capture_path` (`d3d11`, `d3d12`, `gl`, `vk`,
`printwindow`), `w`, `h` and `frame`. `--after-frames N` waits for N more presented frames first (e.g. after an action);
`--region x,y,w,h` crops client pixels (later `--capture-space` coordinates keep that crop's origin).
`--method native` (= `swapchain`) never falls back; `auto` falls back to `PrintWindow` and puts the native error in
`note`. `wait-change --region ... --timeout 5` polls fresh frame hashes and returns on a visual change; a change proves
pixels changed, not that a particular action succeeded.

| path | how the frame is found |
|---|---|
| d3d11 | `Present` hook, staging copy |
| d3d12 | `Present` / `Present1`; the game's DIRECT queue from the `ExecuteCommandLists` hook; own allocator / list / fence copy the back buffer to a readback buffer; the game never waits |
| gl | `wglSwapBuffers` / `SwapBuffers`, `glReadPixels` of the back buffer on the game's GL thread, touched GL state restored |
| vk | `vkQueuePresentKHR` + device / queue / swapchain hooks; copy to a host-visible buffer chained by semaphores; needs injection before the game creates its `VkDevice` (`launch --early`), otherwise a clear refusal and the `PrintWindow` fallback |
| printwindow | `PrintWindow(PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT)`, fallback only |

GL / Vulkan drivers may present through their own internal DXGI swapchain; those presents are recognised as
`foreign_dxgi` and never counted as frames of their own. `config vk=off` makes every Vulkan hook a pass-through.

## UI navigation: by text and by picture

All of this runs in the CLI process (OCR = the built-in `Windows.Media.Ocr` API; image matching = our own code);
nothing extra is loaded into the game. Boxes are `[x,y,w,h]` in client pixels (a capture's region origin and any scale
are applied for you, so a box can be fed straight to `click`).

| command | what it does |
|---|---|
| `ocr [--region ..] [--lang en-US] [--scale 1] [--tiles] [--lines-only] [--out f.json]` | OCR the frame: `text`, `lines[]` and `words[]` with boxes. `--scale 2` upscales first (small text). `--tiles` adds the tiled pass. |
| `click-text "text" [--nth N] [--exact] [--fuzzy N] [--timeout ms] [--button left] [--region ..] [--dry-run] [--optional]` | find the text and click the centre of its box; reply has the matched box, `match_count`, `match_score`. **Several matches and no `--nth` = refuse, click nothing, list the candidates.** `--timeout` (default 5000) keeps polling. `--dry-run` reports without clicking. `--optional` succeeds with `skipped:true` if the text never shows. |
| `wait-text "text" [--timeout ms] [--gone] [--region ..] [--optional]` | block until the text is on screen (default 15000 ms) or, with `--gone`, until it is not. Times out with `timed_out:true` and `ocr_saw`. |
| `assert-text "text" [--absent]` | one look, no waiting. |
| `find-image t.png [--threshold 0.8] [--scales a,b,c \| --no-scale] [--region ..]` | normalised cross-correlation template match; `matches[]` with box, `score`, `scale`. |
| `click-image t.png [--nth N] [--timeout ms] [--dry-run] [--optional]` / `wait-image t.png [--gone]` | same refusal / timeout rules as the text commands. |
| `pixel X Y` | RGB (+ `#RRGGBB`) of one client pixel. |
| `scroll N [X Y]` | N wheel notches (positive = up / away) at the virtual cursor, after moving it to X Y if given. |
| `drag x1 y1 x2 y2 [--ms 300] [--button left]` | press at 1, move with the button held, release at 2 (always releases). |
| `script file [--continue]` | run a macro (below). |

**Matching rules.** Default: case-insensitive, all whitespace ignored on both sides (`LoadGame` finds `Load   Game`),
substring of a line (`PLAY` also hits `PLAYERS`). `--exact`: case-sensitive and the match must start and end on OCR word
boundaries. `--fuzzy N` (0..3) also accepts whole-word runs within N edits (OCR slips); those hits have
`match_score` < 1. `--nth N` is 1-based in reading order. `ocr_confidence` is always `null`: the Windows engine reports
none, and none is invented.

**OCR is not stable, so the search is layered.** Windows OCR's layout analysis can drop words from a full frame that it
reads fine in a crop. Text commands therefore try: full frame at 1x, then a 2x3 overlapping tiled pass, then the same at
2x, and stop at the first pass that matches (~0.1 s, ~0.6 s with fallback). Stylised or very small text: use `--region`,
`--scale 2`, or `click-image`. If a label also appears elsewhere, confine the search with `--region`.

**Image matching** is zero-mean NCC on greyscale, so brightness / contrast changes do not matter. It tries scales
0.85 0.92 1.0 1.08 1.18; copies more than about +-20 % different in size are not found unless you widen `--scales`. No
rotation. A flat (single-colour) template is refused. Self-similar templates (stripes, nested squares) can correlate
with a wrong-scale copy at ~0.84: raise `--threshold` to 0.9+.

### Cookbook

```
vinput --pid N click-text "Load Game"
vinput --pid N wait-text "Select a save" --timeout 10000

vinput --pid N click-text BATTLE --nth 2                  # two buttons say the same thing: pick by position
vinput --pid N click-text BATTLE --region 400,570,480,110 # or confine the search

vinput --pid N wait-text "Loading" --gone --timeout 120000
vinput --pid N capture icon.png --region 1205,290,70,140  # icon-only button: capture it once ...
vinput --pid N click-image icon.png --threshold 0.9       # ... then click by picture
```

### Scripts

A `.vin` script has one command per line (no `--pid`), `#` comments, `sleep ms`, `echo text`. It stops at the first
failing line and prints its number; relative paths resolve against the script's folder; `--continue` runs on and still
exits 1. Example (`macros/synthetic_menu_to_game.vin`, for the synthetic target `test/vi_uitarget.cpp`):

```
assert-text "MAIN MENU" --timeout 10000
click-text PLAY
wait-text "Select a game type" --timeout 8000
click-text SOLO
wait-text "Game started" --timeout 8000
```

`vinput --pid N script macros\synthetic_menu_to_game.vin` prints one JSON line per command and a final summary
(`{"ok":false,"error":"script failed at line 5",...,"first_failure":{...}}` on failure).

```

`macros/synthetic_menu_to_game.vin`:

```vin
# Synthetic test target (test\vi_uitarget.cpp): main menu -> PLAY -> Select screen -> SOLO -> game.
# Run:  vinput --pid N script macros\synthetic_menu_to_game.vin
assert-text "MAIN MENU" --timeout 10000
click-text PLAY
wait-text "Select a game type" --timeout 8000
click-text SOLO
wait-text "Game started" --timeout 8000
echo reached the game screen

```

`macros/synthetic_pick_second_battle.vin`:

```vin
# Two identical BATTLE buttons: pick the right-hand one explicitly, then confirm with a pixel read is not needed -
# the macro simply proves --nth works from a script. Fails (and stops) if BATTLE is not on screen.
wait-text "MAIN MENU" --timeout 10000
click-text BATTLE --nth 2
sleep 200
click-text "Load Game"

```

`mcp/README.md`:

```md
# llm-game-automation-mcp - MCP server

> **Single-player / offline games only.** It injects a DLL into the game. Never point it at online / multiplayer games
> or games with anti-cheat. See [../DISCLAIMER.md](../DISCLAIMER.md).

A [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server (stdio transport, official
`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`) that lets any LLM agent play Windows games through vinput: input and screenshots go to
one game process **in the background**, so the game never needs focus and you keep your mouse and keyboard.

Each tool runs `vinput.exe` and returns **vinput's own JSON reply** as text. `ok` is surfaced as the MCP `isError`
flag: `ok:false` (or a crash, timeout or missing binary) always comes back as `isError: true` with the error text,
never silently. `capture` also returns the PNG as MCP image content.

## Build

Requires Windows 10/11 x64, Node.js 20+, and the vinput binaries (`build.bat` in the repository root).

```bat
cd mcp
npm ci
npm run build
npm test          &rem handshake: starts build\index.js, initialize + tools/list, checks every schema
npm run smoke     &rem live end-to-end run against the synthetic test target (needs build.bat output)
```

## Configure your client

The server finds `vinput.exe` at `<repo>\dist\vinput.exe`. Environment variables (all optional):

| variable | meaning |
|---|---|
| `VINPUT_EXE` | path of `vinput.exe` if it is somewhere else |
| `VINPUT_CAPTURE_DIR` | where `capture` saves PNGs when no path is given (default `<repo>\captures`) |
| `VINPUT_OWNER` | owner name for vinput's per-game claims (default `mcp-<server pid>`) |
| `VINPUT_MCP_MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` | larger captures are saved but not attached as images (default 8 MiB) |

**Claude Code**

```bat
claude mcp add game-automation -- node C:\path\to\llm-game-automation-mcp\mcp\build\index.js
```

**Claude Desktop** - `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "game-automation": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["C:\\path\\to\\llm-game-automation-mcp\\mcp\\build\\index.js"],
      "env": { "VINPUT_CAPTURE_DIR": "C:\\path\\to\\captures" }
    }
  }
}
```

**Any other MCP client** - start a stdio server with command `node` and argument
`C:\path\to\llm-game-automation-mcp\mcp\build\index.js`. It speaks MCP over stdin/stdout and logs only to stderr.

## Agent quick start

```
1. launch {exe:"C:\\Games\\X\\X.exe", args:"-windowed"}      -> remember pid   (or attach {pid} / list_targets)
2. capture {pid}                                               -> look at the image (pixels = click coordinates)
3. wait_text {pid, text:"New Game"}                            -> make sure the screen is ready
4. click_text {pid, text:"New Game"}                           -> act by text; several matches = refusal, add nth
5. wait_text {pid, text:"Difficulty"} or wait_change {pid}     -> verify; ok:true on input only means "delivered"
6. click {pid, x, y} / key {pid, key:"enter"} / pad {pid, buttons:"a"}   -> other actions
7. key {pid, key:"w", hold_ms:1500}; move_relative {pid, dx:200, dy:0}   -> walk / look in 3D games
8. capture {pid, after_frames:3}                               -> look again after acting
9. status {pid}                                                -> counters show which input APIs the game reads
10. release {pid}; detach {pid}                                -> stop driving; the game keeps running
```

## Tools

| tool | what it does |
|---|---|
| `launch` | start a game (`exe` / `aumid` / `steam_appid`+`wait_exe`, `args`, `early`, `settle_s`, `timeout_s`, `lock`, `claim`) and inject; returns `pid` |
| `attach` | inject into a running game by `pid` and wait until its window is adopted |
| `list_targets` | games that have vinput loaded (pid, exe, owner, uptime, really_foreground) |
| `status` | window, client size, capture path, claim, input-API counters |
| `capture` | the game's own frame as an image + `{path, w, h, method, capture_path, frame}`; `region`, `after_frames`, `method`, `include_image` |
| `ocr` | text and lines with boxes (`region`, `scale`, `lang`, `words`, `tiles`) |
| `find_text` | locate text without clicking (box, centre, match_count) |
| `click_text` | find text and click its centre (`nth`, `exact`, `fuzzy`, `timeout_ms`, `button`, `region`, `optional`) |
| `wait_text` | wait until text appears (or `gone`) |
| `find_image` / `click_image` / `wait_image` | template matching with a PNG (`threshold`, `scales`, `region`, `nth`) |
| `pixel` | colour of one pixel |
| `wait_change` | wait until the picture (or a region) changes |
| `click` | click at `x`,`y` (client pixels, or `norm` 0..1, or `capture_space`), `button`, `count`, `hold_ms` |
| `move` | move the virtual cursor (hover) |
| `move_relative` | relative mouse motion for mouse-look (`dx`, `dy`, `raw`) |
| `drag` | press, move, release |
| `scroll` | wheel notches at the cursor or at `x`,`y` |
| `key` | press a key or chord (`hold_ms`, `count`, `gap_ms`) |
| `key_down` / `key_up` | hold / release a key (or mouse button name) |
| `type_text` | type Unicode text (`as_keys` for games that read raw keys) |
| `pad` | XInput pad 0: `buttons`, sticks `lx ly rx ry`, triggers `lt rt`, `ms`, `hold`, `off` |
| `list_keys` | all key names |
| `run_script` | run a `.vin` macro file |
| `release` | release all held input |
| `detach` | release input and drop this server's claim (vinput stays loaded, inert, until the game exits) |

Every tool that targets a game takes `pid`. Coordinates are the game's **client pixels**, which equal the pixels of a
full capture. Refusals by the anti-cheat check come back as `isError` with `anticheat_refused: true`; there is no way to
override them from the MCP server.

## Notes for agents

- **Verify every action.** `ok:true` from `click`, `key` or `click_text` means the input reached the game, not that the
  game did what you wanted. Use `wait_text`, `wait_change` or a new `capture`.
- **Text matching** is case-insensitive, ignores whitespace and matches substrings of a line. If a label appears more
  than once, `click_text` refuses and lists candidates: pass `nth` or a `region`.
- **OCR misses** small or stylised text: use `region` + `scale: 2`, or cut an icon from a capture and use
  `click_image`.
- **3D games** often read raw input: walk with `key` + `hold_ms`, look with `move_relative`; check `status` counters
  if nothing happens. UWP games often ignore keyboard messages but read XInput: use `pad`.
- **Big captures** cost tokens: capture a `region` when you only need part of the screen.

```

`mcp/src/index.ts`:

```ts
#!/usr/bin/env node
// llm-game-automation-mcp: an MCP (stdio) server that lets an LLM agent play single-player / offline Windows games
// through vinput. Every tool runs the vinput CLI and returns its JSON reply verbatim, with "ok" surfaced as isError.
// Offline games only: vinput injects a DLL and refuses targets with a known anti-cheat (see DISCLAIMER.md).
import { readFileSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
import { resolve } from "node:path";
import { McpServer } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/mcp.js";
import { StdioServerTransport } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/stdio.js";
import { z } from "zod";
import { CliResult, defaultCapturePath, resolveVinputExe, runVinput } from "./vinput.js";

const VERSION = "0.1.0";
const OWNER = (process.env.VINPUT_OWNER ?? "").trim() || `mcp-${process.pid}`;
const MAX_IMAGE_BYTES = Number(process.env.VINPUT_MCP_MAX_IMAGE_BYTES ?? 8 * 1024 * 1024);

type Content = { type: "text"; text: string } | { type: "image"; data: string; mimeType: string };
type ToolReply = { content: Content[]; isError?: boolean };

function reply(r: CliResult, extra?: Record<string, unknown>): ToolReply {
  let json = r.json;
  if (extra && json && typeof json === "object" && !Array.isArray(json)) json = { ...(json as object), ...extra };
  const content: Content[] = [{ type: "text", text: JSON.stringify(json) }];
  if (!r.ok && r.stderr) content.push({ type: "text", text: `vinput stderr:\n${r.stderr.slice(-4000)}` });
  return { content, isError: !r.ok };
}
function fail(message: string): ToolReply {
  return { content: [{ type: "text", text: JSON.stringify({ ok: false, error: message }) }], isError: true };
}

/** argv prefix for a command aimed at one game process */
const at = (pid: number) => ["--owner", OWNER, "--pid", String(pid)];
const region = (r?: { x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number }) => (r ? ["--region", `${r.x},${r.y},${r.w},${r.h}`] : []);
const opt = (flag: string, v: unknown) => (v === undefined || v === null || v === false ? [] : v === true ? [flag] : [flag, String(v)]);

const pid = z.number().int().positive().describe("Process id of the game, as returned by launch / attach / list_targets.");
const regionSchema = z.object({
  x: z.number().int().min(0), y: z.number().int().min(0), w: z.number().int().positive(), h: z.number().int().positive(),
}).describe("Rectangle in client pixels (same as capture pixels): x, y = top-left corner, w, h = size.");
const button = z.enum(["left", "right", "middle", "x1", "x2"]);
const timeoutMs = (def: number) => z.number().int().min(0).max(600000).optional().describe(`How long to keep looking, in ms (default ${def}).`);

const server = new McpServer(
  { name: "llm-game-automation-mcp", version: VERSION },
  {
    instructions:
      "Plays single-player / offline Windows games through vinput: input and screenshots go to ONE game process in the " +
      "background, so the game never needs focus and the user keeps the mouse and keyboard. Workflow: launch (or attach) -> " +
      "capture to look -> act (click_text / click / key / pad) -> verify with wait_text, capture or wait_change. " +
      "Coordinates are the game's client pixels, which equal the pixels of a full capture. ok:true on an input tool only " +
      "means the input was delivered, not that the game reacted: always verify. Never use it on online / multiplayer games " +
      "or games with anti-cheat; vinput refuses targets with a known anti-cheat and that refusal cannot be overridden.",
  },
);

function tool<S extends z.ZodRawShape>(name: string, title: string, description: string, shape: S,
  run: (a: z.objectOutputType<S, z.ZodTypeAny>) => Promise<ToolReply>, readOnly = false) {
  server.registerTool(name, { title, description, inputSchema: shape, annotations: { title, readOnlyHint: readOnly, openWorldHint: false } },
    // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
    (async (a: any) => {
      try { return await run(a); } catch (e) { return fail(`${name}: ${(e as Error).message}`); }
    }) as never);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- targets
tool("launch", "Launch a game",
  "Start a game and inject vinput into it. Returns {ok, pid, injected, foreground_restored, ...}; keep the pid for every " +
  "other tool. Give exactly one of exe (a .exe path), aumid (a UWP / Xbox app id 'PackageFamilyName!AppId') or " +
  "steam_appid (+ wait_exe). Run games WINDOWED or borderless (exclusive fullscreen breaks background capture). Use " +
  "early:true for Vulkan / OpenGL games so capture hooks are in before the device is created (exe only). Refused with " +
  "anticheat_refused:true if the game or the machine has a known anti-cheat.",
  {
    exe: z.string().optional().describe("Full path of the game executable."),
    args: z.string().optional().describe("Command line arguments for the game, e.g. \"-windowed -width 1280 -height 720\"."),
    aumid: z.string().optional().describe("UWP / Xbox app user model id, e.g. 'Publisher.Game_abc123!App'."),
    steam_appid: z.string().optional().describe("Steam app id; starts the game through Steam (needs wait_exe)."),
    wait_exe: z.string().optional().describe("Executable name to wait for, e.g. 'Game-Win64-Shipping.exe' (launchers, Steam relaunches)."),
    early: z.boolean().optional().describe("Create the process suspended and inject before its first instruction (exe only)."),
    settle_s: z.number().min(0).max(600).optional().describe("Seconds to let the game settle after injection (default 5)."),
    timeout_s: z.number().min(1).max(1800).optional().describe("Seconds to wait for the game window (default 240)."),
    lock: z.string().optional().describe("Optional lock file shared by tools that may touch the real foreground; held only while launching."),
    claim: z.boolean().optional().describe("Claim the game for this MCP server so other vinput clients are refused (default false)."),
  },
  async (a) => {
    const n = [a.exe, a.aumid, a.steam_appid].filter((v) => v).length;
    if (n !== 1) return fail("give exactly one of exe, aumid or steam_appid");
    const argv = ["--owner", OWNER, "launch",
      ...opt("--exe", a.exe), ...opt("--aumid", a.aumid), ...opt("--steam", a.steam_appid), ...opt("--wait-exe", a.wait_exe),
      ...opt("--args", a.args), ...opt("--early", a.early), ...opt("--settle", a.settle_s), ...opt("--timeout", a.timeout_s),
      ...opt("--lock", a.lock)];
    const r = await runVinput(argv, ((a.timeout_s ?? 240) + (a.settle_s ?? 5) + 120) * 1000);
    if (r.ok && a.claim) {
      const p = (r.json as { pid?: number }).pid;
      if (p) { const c = await runVinput([...at(p), "claim", "--ttl", "3600"], 15000); return reply(r, { claim: c.json }); }
    }
    return reply(r);
  });

tool("attach", "Attach to a running game",
  "Inject vinput into an already running game by process id (32- and 64-bit). Returns the game's status. Refused with " +
  "anticheat_refused:true if the game or the machine has a known anti-cheat. Use list_targets to see games that already have vinput.",
  { pid, claim: z.boolean().optional().describe("Claim the game for this MCP server (default false).") },
  async (a) => {
    const r = await runVinput(["inject", "--pid", String(a.pid)], 60000);
    if (!r.ok) return reply(r);
    if (a.claim) await runVinput([...at(a.pid), "claim", "--ttl", "3600"], 15000);
    for (let i = 0; i < 50; i++) {
      const s = await runVinput([...at(a.pid), "status"], 15000);
      const hwnd = (s.json as { hwnd?: string }).hwnd;
      if (!s.ok || (hwnd && hwnd !== "0x0") || i === 49) return reply(s, { injected: true });
      await new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, 200));
    }
    return fail("unreachable");
  });

tool("list_targets", "List controllable games",
  "List every process that currently has vinput loaded: pid, exe, owner (claim), uptime, really_foreground, responding.",
  {}, async () => {
    const r = await runVinput(["list"], 30000);
    return reply({ ...r, json: Array.isArray(r.json) ? { ok: r.ok, targets: r.json } : r.json });
  }, true);

tool("status", "Game status",
  "vinput status of one game: window, client size, capture path in use, really_foreground, claim, and counters showing " +
  "which input APIs the game actually reads (read these when the game ignores input).",
  { pid }, async (a) => reply(await runVinput([...at(a.pid), "status"], 15000)), true);

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- eyes
tool("capture", "Capture a frame",
  "Screenshot of the game's own frame (D3D11/D3D12/OpenGL/Vulkan swapchain, PrintWindow fallback) taken in the background. " +
  "Returns the PNG as an image plus JSON {path, w, h, method, capture_path, frame}. Image pixels = client pixels, so " +
  "coordinates you read off the image can be passed straight to click / move. With region, the image is that crop; " +
  "pass capture_space:true to click / move to use coordinates inside the crop.",
  {
    pid,
    path: z.string().optional().describe("Where to save the PNG (default: a new file in the captures folder)."),
    region: regionSchema.optional(),
    after_frames: z.number().int().min(0).max(3600).optional().describe("Wait for this many new presented frames first (e.g. 3 after an action)."),
    method: z.enum(["auto", "native", "printwindow"]).optional().describe("auto (default) falls back to PrintWindow and says why in 'note'."),
    include_image: z.boolean().optional().describe("Return the image content (default true). False = path + JSON only."),
  },
  async (a) => {
    const path = resolve(a.path ?? defaultCapturePath(a.pid));
    const r = await runVinput([...at(a.pid), "capture", path, ...region(a.region), ...opt("--after-frames", a.after_frames), ...opt("--method", a.method === "native" ? "swapchain" : a.method)], 60000);
    const out = reply(r);
    if (r.ok && a.include_image !== false) {
      const saved = ((r.json as { path?: string }).path) || path;
      try {
        const size = statSync(saved).size;
        if (size > MAX_IMAGE_BYTES) out.content.push({ type: "text", text: `image not attached: ${size} bytes > ${MAX_IMAGE_BYTES}; use region to capture less` });
        else out.content.push({ type: "image", data: readFileSync(saved).toString("base64"), mimeType: "image/png" });
      } catch (e) { out.content.push({ type: "text", text: `capture reported ok but the PNG could not be read: ${(e as Error).message}` }); out.isError = true; }
    }
    return out;
  });

tool("ocr", "Read text on screen",
  "OCR the current frame with the built-in Windows OCR engine. Returns text and lines[] with boxes [x,y,w,h] in client " +
  "pixels (words[] too when words:true). Small or stylised text: use region and scale 2.",
  {
    pid, region: regionSchema.optional(),
    scale: z.number().min(1).max(4).optional().describe("Upscale before OCR (2 helps small text)."),
    lang: z.string().optional().describe("OCR language tag, e.g. en-US (default: the user's profile language)."),
    words: z.boolean().optional().describe("Also return every word with its box (bigger reply)."),
    tiles: z.boolean().optional().describe("Tiled second pass that finds words the full-frame pass drops (default true; false is faster)."),
  },
  async (a) => reply(await runVinput([...at(a.pid), "ocr", ...region(a.region), ...opt("--scale", a.scale), ...opt("--lang", a.lang),
    ...(a.words ? [] : ["--lines-only"]), ...(a.tiles === false ? [] : ["--tiles"])], 60000)), true);

const textMatch = {
  text: z.string().min(1).describe("Text to find. Default matching: case-insensitive, whitespace ignored, substring of a line."),
  nth: z.number().int().min(1).optional().describe("Pick the Nth match in reading order (1-based). Without it, several matches = refusal listing the candidates."),
  exact: z.boolean().optional().describe("Case-sensitive, whole-word match."),
  fuzzy: z.number().int().min(0).max(3).optional().describe("Also accept whole words within N edits (OCR slips)."),
  region: regionSchema.optional(),
};
const textArgs = (a: { text: string; nth?: number; exact?: boolean; fuzzy?: number; region?: z.infer<typeof regionSchema> }) =>
  [a.text, ...opt("--nth", a.nth), ...opt("--exact", a.exact), ...opt("--fuzzy", a.fuzzy), ...region(a.region)];

tool("find_text", "Find text on screen",
  "Locate text without clicking. Returns the matched box, centre, match_count and match_score, or ok:false (with what OCR " +
  "did read) when it is not there.",
  { pid, ...textMatch, timeout_ms: timeoutMs(0) },
  async (a) => reply(await runVinput([...at(a.pid), "click-text", ...textArgs(a), "--dry-run", "--timeout", String(a.timeout_ms ?? 0)], (a.timeout_ms ?? 0) + 60000)), true);

tool("click_text", "Click text on screen",
  "Find text with OCR and click the centre of its box (keeps looking for timeout_ms). Refuses and clicks nothing when " +
  "the text matches more than once and nth is not given. Verify the result with wait_text / capture.",
  { pid, ...textMatch, timeout_ms: timeoutMs(5000), button: button.optional(),
    optional: z.boolean().optional().describe("Succeed with skipped:true if the text never appears (for dialogs that may not show).") },
  async (a) => reply(await runVinput([...at(a.pid), "click-text", ...textArgs(a), ...opt("--timeout", a.timeout_ms), ...opt("--button", a.button),
    ...opt("--optional", a.optional)], (a.timeout_ms ?? 5000) + 60000)));

tool("wait_text", "Wait for text",
  "Block until text appears on screen (or, with gone:true, disappears). Times out with timed_out:true and ocr_saw.",
  { pid, text: textMatch.text, region: regionSchema.optional(), gone: z.boolean().optional().describe("Wait until the text is NOT on screen."),
    timeout_ms: timeoutMs(15000), optional: z.boolean().optional().describe("Succeed with skipped:true on timeout.") },
  async (a) => reply(await runVinput([...at(a.pid), "wait-text", a.text, ...region(a.region), ...opt("--gone", a.gone),
    ...opt("--timeout", a.timeout_ms), ...opt("--optional", a.optional)], (a.timeout_ms ?? 15000) + 60000)), true);

const imageArgs = {
  template: z.string().min(1).describe("Path of a PNG template (e.g. an icon cut from an earlier capture with region)."),
  threshold: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional().describe("Match score needed, 0..1 (default 0.8; use 0.9+ for repetitive patterns)."),
  scales: z.string().optional().describe("Comma-separated scales to try, e.g. '0.9,1,1.1' (default 0.85..1.18)."),
  region: regionSchema.optional(),
};
const imgArgv = (a: { template: string; threshold?: number; scales?: string; region?: z.infer<typeof regionSchema> }) =>
  [resolve(a.template), ...opt("--threshold", a.threshold), ...opt("--scales", a.scales), ...region(a.region)];

tool("find_image", "Find an image on screen",
  "Template-match a PNG on the current frame (normalised cross-correlation, brightness-independent, no rotation). " +
  "Returns matches[] with box, score and scale.",
  { pid, ...imageArgs }, async (a) => reply(await runVinput([...at(a.pid), "find-image", ...imgArgv(a)], 60000)), true);

tool("click_image", "Click an image on screen",
  "Find a PNG template on screen and click its centre. Refuses when it matches more than once and nth is not given.",
  { pid, ...imageArgs, nth: z.number().int().min(1).optional(), timeout_ms: timeoutMs(5000), button: button.optional(),
    optional: z.boolean().optional() },
  async (a) => reply(await runVinput([...at(a.pid), "click-image", ...imgArgv(a), ...opt("--nth", a.nth), ...opt("--timeout", a.timeout_ms),
    ...opt("--button", a.button), ...opt("--optional", a.optional)], (a.timeout_ms ?? 5000) + 60000)));

tool("wait_image", "Wait for an image",
  "Block until a PNG template appears on screen (or disappears with gone:true).",
  { pid, ...imageArgs, gone: z.boolean().optional(), timeout_ms: timeoutMs(15000) },
  async (a) => reply(await runVinput([...at(a.pid), "wait-image", ...imgArgv(a), ...opt("--gone", a.gone), ...opt("--timeout", a.timeout_ms)],
    (a.timeout_ms ?? 15000) + 60000)), true);

tool("pixel", "Read one pixel", "RGB colour of one client pixel: {r,g,b,hex}.",
  { pid, x: z.number().int().min(0), y: z.number().int().min(0) },

  async (a) => reply(await runVinput([...at(a.pid), "wait-change", ...region(a.region), ...opt("--timeout", a.timeout_s)], ((a.timeout_s ?? 10) + 60) * 1000)), true);

  x: z.number().describe("X in client pixels (or 0..1 with norm)."),

    if (a.as_keys) cmd.keys = true;

  });

  "stops overriding the pad.",
  { pid, buttons: z.string().optional().describe("e.g. 'a', 'a+b', 'down', 'none'."),
    ms: z.number().int().min(1).max(60000).optional(),
    lx: z.number().int().min(-32768).max(32767).optional(), ly: z.number().int().min(-32768).max(32767).optional(),
    rx: z.number().int().min(-32768).max(32767).optional(), ry: z.number().int().min(-32768).max(32767).optional(),
    lt: z.number().int().min(0).max(255).optional(), rt: z.number().int().min(0).max(255).optional(),
    hold: z.boolean().optional(), off: z.boolean().optional() },

    return reply(await runVinput([...at(a.pid), "pad", a.buttons ?? "none", ...(a.ms ? [String(a.ms)] : []),
      ...opt("--lx", a.lx), ...opt("--ly", a.ly), ...opt("--rx", a.rx), ...opt("--ry", a.ry), ...opt("--lt", a.lt), ...opt("--rt", a.rt),
      ...opt("--hold", a.hold)], (a.ms ?? 0) + 60000));
  });

tool("list_keys", "List key names", "Every key name vinput accepts, with its virtual-key code.", {},
  async () => reply(await runVinput(["keys"], 15000)), true);

tool("run_script", "Run a macro script",
  "Run a .vin macro on the game: one vinput command per line (no --pid), '#' comments, 'sleep ms'. Stops at the first failing line unless continue_on_error.",
  { pid, file: z.string().min(1), continue_on_error: z.boolean().optional(), timeout_s: z.number().min(1).max(3600).optional() },
  async (a) => reply(await runVinput([...at(a.pid), "script", resolve(a.file), ...opt("--continue", a.continue_on_error)], (a.timeout_s ?? 600) * 1000)));

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- release
tool("release", "Release all input",
  "Release every key, mouse button and pad input this server is holding in the game.",
  { pid }, async (a) => reply(await runVinput([...at(a.pid), "release"], 30000)));

tool("detach", "Stop controlling a game",
  "Release all input and drop this server's claim. vinput stays loaded (inert) until the game exits; the game keeps running.",
  { pid }, async (a) => {
    const rel = await runVinput([...at(a.pid), "release"], 30000);
    const un = await runVinput([...at(a.pid), "unclaim"], 30000);
    return reply(rel, { unclaim: un.json, note: "vinput stays loaded until the game exits; no further input is sent" });
  });

async function main() {
  const transport = new StdioServerTransport();
  await server.connect(transport);
  process.stderr.write(`llm-game-automation-mcp ${VERSION} ready (vinput: ${resolveVinputExe()}, owner: ${OWNER})\n`);
}
main().catch((e) => { process.stderr.write(`fatal: ${(e as Error).stack ?? e}\n`); process.exit(1); });
